provenance: [REVIEWED] research/v3/ORACLE_QUESTION_SET.md v2 §A.6. Committed a priori, before any probe-arm inference exists. The enumeration below is generated from `rules_in_order` and is the contract: an implementation that disagrees with any of the 729 entries is wrong, not the table.
encoding: Each key is six characters over {y,n,u}, one per probe, in `probe_order`. y=yes, n=no, u=unsure.
unsure_policy: `unsure` is never an assertion. It triggers no rule. It is counted (see `unsure_rate` in the analysis contract) and it can only ever route a vector to rule 9.

rules_in_order.if: bg_visible == no AND any of (one_colour, continuous_change, separate_areas, motif_or_material, depicted_place) == yes
rules_in_order.why: You cannot see no background and also describe it.
The escape hatch, reached only when nothing contradicts it.

rules_in_order.if: one_colour == yes AND (continuous_change == yes OR separate_areas == yes)
rules_in_order.why: One colour all over cannot also change across itself or be several colours.

rules_in_order.tension: uniform_vs_material when motif_or_material == yes — a one-colour paper or canvas is real; flat_field wins and field_texture carries the material.

rules_in_order.why: Continuity wins. The probe asks for change across the WHOLE background, so the competing cases (gradient sky over flat grass, flat area meeting shaded area) answer `no` here and never reach this rule. See §A.6.4's six worked cases.
Discrete colour areas beat both material and depicted place. This is the full_scene leak closed a priori: sky over grass is two areas that happen to be photographed.
A motif or material that is the ground, with no colour structure asserted.
Reached only when no colour-structure probe fired — which IS v2's definition sentence for full_scene: a depicted space with no readable colour behaviour.

rules_in_order.disposition: unsure if any probe == unsure, else all_negative
rules_in_order.why: Nothing was asserted. There is nothing to derive from, and saying so is the point.

field_texture_derivation: NOTE the deliberate asymmetry with ground_type: material beats areas here, areas beat material there. field_texture is about the material question; ground_type is about colour structure. §A.6.5.
shading_geometry_derivation: Take shading_direction as answered, then force not_applicable when the derived ground_type is not shaded_field.

Report both the raw and the forced value. In group-a.v1 the radial_or_vignette<->not_applicable pair was 21 of 26 inter-variant disagreements on this field [MEASURED premise-run-1]; forcing removes that class by construction rather than by asking better.

self_check.note: These counts are over the uniform 3^6 vector space, NOT over any corpus. They exist to prove the table is total, that every tag is reachable, and that no tag is degenerate. They are not a prediction.
